topic: First-principles calculations map the band gap of lead-iodide perovskites APbI3 (corner-sharing PbI6 octahedra with a cation A in the cavities) across many real and hypothetical cations.

facts.text: Band structures computed with and without the cation agree near the gap; the cation states lie several eV away from the band edges.

In the measured structures of methylammonium lead iodide the Pb-I bond lengths deviate by at most 0.1 per cent from their average of 3.18 A, and the diagonals of each octahedron are within 4 degrees of perpendicular.

A model built from perfectly regular corner-sharing octahedra with no cation at all reproduces a gap that varies by up to about 1 eV with the Pb-I-Pb bond angles, following the largest of those angles.
At fixed bond angles, the spread of Pb-I bond lengths among the realistic structures changes the gap by about 0.2 eV (roughly 3 eV per angstrom).

ask: Which explanation of how the cation tunes the band gap is consistent with all of these facts?

hypotheses.text: The gap is set by the largest Pb-I-Pb bond angle, that is by the octahedral tilt; the cation acts only through its steric size, by controlling that tilt.
hypotheses.locator: Abstract and Fig. 3b: the gap correlates with the largest metal-halide-metal bond angle, tuned through the steric size of the cation
hypotheses.reason: 与全部观测一致，即原文结论。

hypotheses.text: The orbitals of the cation form the band edges and set the gap directly.
hypotheses.locator: Fig. 1b: the cation states are far from the gap
hypotheses.reason: 去掉阳离子后带隙附近的能带几乎不变，说明带边不是阳离子轨道。

hypotheses.text: Changes of the Pb-I bond length dominate the gap.
hypotheses.locator: Fig. 2 caption: bond-length spread accounts for about 0.2 eV
hypotheses.reason: 键长差异只带来约 0.2 eV，而键角变化可达约 1 eV。

hypotheses.text: Distortion of the PbI6 octahedra themselves dominates the gap.
hypotheses.locator: Main text p. 2: the measured octahedra are regular to within 0.1 per cent and 4 degrees
hypotheses.reason: 实测八面体几乎正则，而且完全正则的八面体模型已能重现带隙随键角的变化。
